text: I moved to Canada six months ago. I have stopped attending classes, I am scared to tell my parents, and I cannot sleep before exams.
notes: The worked example from the project brief. No single phrase is alarming; the acuity comes from three domains failing at once.

text: I have not opened my laptop for my dissertation in three weeks. Every time I try I feel sick and end up watching something instead. My supervisor has emailed twice and I have not replied.
notes: Avoidance described behaviourally rather than named. Tests whether the engine needs the literal phrase stopped attending.

text: I am on academic probation and if I fail one more module they will report me to the Home Office. My attendance is at forty percent.
notes: Academic risk with a visa consequence. Should stay academic as primary with visa as secondary, not flip.

text: My grades have slipped from distinction to barely passing. I keep telling myself I will catch up next week and then I do not.

It has been eight months and I still eat every meal alone. People at work are polite but I have not been invited to anything. I did not realise how much I relied on just bumping into people back home.
notes: Loneliness in a professional, not a student. Tests that the professional prior does not force a work category.

text: I am homesick constantly. I call my mother every day and cry after. I have not made a single friend here.
notes: Mentions mother but the issue is isolation, not parental pressure.

text: The culture shock has been worse than I expected. I do not understand the humour, I do not drink, and every social thing here happens in a pub.
notes: Cultural rather than clinical. Should not be routed to identity/discrimination since nobody is mistreating them.

text: I have not left my room except for groceries in about three weeks. I do not really speak to anyone. I am not sad exactly, just switched off.
notes: Withdrawal with flat affect. Genuinely ambiguous between isolation and clinical; either primary is defensible but it must reach a human.

text: I have been put on a performance improvement plan with thirty days to turn things around. I am the only one on my team on a sponsored visa so I cannot just leave.
notes: PIP plus visa dependency. Work primary, visa secondary.

text: I work twelve hour days and still feel behind. I have started making mistakes I would never have made a year ago and I am terrified someone will notice.
Everyone on my team went to a better university than me and I keep waiting to be found out. I rehearse what I will say in meetings for hours and then say nothing.
notes: Imposter syndrome without the phrase. Mentions university, which is an academic distractor.

text: I was laid off on Tuesday. I have sixty days to find something or I have to leave the country. I have not told my wife yet.
notes: Layoff is the trigger but the sixty-day clock is the emergency. Work-performance would be a defensible miss; visa is the better route.

text: My manager rewrites everything I do and copies his boss on the corrections. Last week he corrected my English in front of the whole team.
notes: Sits between manager conflict and discrimination. Correcting English in public is plausibly both; manager conflict is primary, discrimination a reasonable secondary.

text: I raised a complaint with HR about my team lead and now I am excluded from the meetings I used to run. Nobody has said anything directly.
My boss keeps hinting that my visa extension depends on me being a team player, and then asks me to work weekends.
notes: Coercion using visa status. Escalates to high. Not a safety flag but a power abuse a coordinator should see.

text: My permit application was refused and the appeal window closes in nine days. I cannot think about anything else and I have stopped eating properly.
notes: Hard deadline plus somatic impact.

text: I have been waiting fourteen months for a decision on my PR. I cannot plan anything, I cannot visit my father who is unwell, and I feel like my life is on hold.
notes: Contains an unwell father, which is a grief distractor. The father is not dying; grief would be a mis-route.

text: My study permit expires next month and my university has been slow with the paperwork. I keep imagining being sent back and having to explain it to everyone.
My partner and I have been arguing constantly since I moved here for work. She thinks I chose the job over her and maybe she is right.
We were together four years and she ended it over a video call last month. I have not told anyone at home because they were about to meet her family.
notes: Breakup with a family-disclosure element. Relationship primary, family secondary.

text: My husband and I moved here together but he got a job and I did not. Now every conversation turns into a fight about money and whose career mattered more.
notes: Money appears but the presenting issue is the relationship.

text: My parents sold part of their land to pay my tuition. I switched courses and have not told them. Every phone call I lie a little more.
notes: Financial sacrifice framing. Family pressure primary, financial secondary.

text: Every call from home is about when I am getting married. I am twenty nine and my mother cries on the phone. I have started not picking up.
I want to tell my parents I am not going to be a doctor. I have wanted to tell them for two years. I practise the sentence and then I cannot say it.
My father said he would stop speaking to me if I do not come back after graduation. He has not called in six weeks.
notes: Threatened estrangement should raise urgency.

text: I have completely flipped my body clock. I am awake until five in the morning and asleep until the afternoon. I miss every morning commitment.
I lie down at eleven and I am still awake at four running through everything I said that day. Then I sleep through my alarm and the whole day is wasted.
notes: Insomnia described without the word insomnia or the phrase cannot sleep.

text: Night shifts have destroyed any routine I had. I eat at odd hours, I have stopped going to the gym, and I feel like a ghost.
My grandmother died three weeks ago and I could not go home for the funeral. I watched it on a video call at two in the morning. I have not really talked about it since.
notes: The specific diaspora grief of attending a funeral by video.

text: My father was diagnosed with something serious last month. I am the eldest and I am eight thousand kilometres away and useless.
notes: Anticipatory grief. The word died never appears.

text: I lost my job, then my flat, and my relationship ended in the same two months. I do not know which one I am upset about anymore.
notes: Uses lost my three times but none are bereavement. Tests the grief exclusion signals against a genuine major-transition case.

text: My education loan repayment starts in four months and I do not have a job offer. My parents have already remortgaged once.
notes: Financial primary with family obligation secondary.

text: I can only legally work twenty hours a week and rent here is more than that covers. I have been skipping meals to make it stretch.
notes: Skipping meals for money reasons. Sleep/routine is a distractor; the driver is financial.

text: I send half my salary home every month and there is never anything left. When my sister asks for more I cannot say no.
notes: Remittance obligation. Genuinely split between financial and family pressure.

text: In every meeting someone says they cannot understand me and asks the person next to me to repeat what I just said. I have started staying quiet.
notes: Accent-based exclusion without the word racism. Easy to mis-route to work performance or manager conflict.

text: Someone shouted at me to go back to my country while I was waiting for the bus. I have not taken that route since and I feel stupid for being shaken.
notes: Racist incident with avoidance behaviour following it.

text: I have anglicised my name on my CV and started getting callbacks. I am relieved and also quietly furious about it.
notes: Structural discrimination, low acuity. Should not be over-escalated just because the topic is racism.

text: I had a panic attack on the train this morning and had to get off two stops early. It is the third one this week. I cannot keep doing this.
notes: Panic attacks escalating in frequency. No risk indicator.

text: I am not okay. I need to speak to someone today. I cannot explain it properly, everything is just too much right now.
notes: Very little content, high distress. Should trigger low-confidence and short-intake review rather than a confident guess.

text: I have been crying every day for two weeks and I cannot point at a reason. I am functioning at work but the moment I close my door I fall apart.
notes: Sustained low mood. Clinical escalation is a defensible alternative label.

text: I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder four years ago and stopped my medication when I moved because I could not find a psychiatrist here.
notes: Medication discontinuation. Must route to a clinically qualified professional, never a coach.

text: I have been making myself sick after meals again. It started at university and I thought I was past it.
notes: Disordered eating described euphemistically. Relapse framing.

text: I have a drink most evenings to get to sleep and lately it is three or four. I do not think it is a problem but my flatmate said something.
notes: Dependent-pattern drinking the user minimises. Should raise an elevated substance flag, not an emergency one.

text: I do not see the point in any of this anymore. I have not told anyone. I just want it to stop.
notes: Passive ideation with no explicit method. Must flag.

text: I have been thinking about ending my life. I have not done anything but the thought is there most days now.
notes: Explicit. Must be caught with no ambiguity.

text: Everyone back home would honestly be better off without me. They have spent so much on me and I have wasted it.
notes: Burden ideation wrapped in family-financial guilt. A category-only classifier would call this family pressure and miss it entirely.

text: I have started cutting again when it gets bad. I keep it hidden and nobody knows.
notes: Self-injury, present tense.

text: My husband took my passport and says I cannot go anywhere without him knowing. He controls all the money. I do not have anyone here.
notes: Coercive control with document confiscation. No violence is named. This is the diaspora-specific abuse pattern most likely to be missed.

text: He hit me on Sunday. It is not the first time. I told work I fell.
I am not safe at home right now. I am messaging from the bathroom. Please can someone call me rather than email.
notes: Short, urgent, contextually alarming.

text: I can hear them talking about me through the walls and I think my flatmates are putting something in my food. I have not slept in four days.
notes: Persecutory ideation plus four days without sleep.

text: I took a handful of my flatmates pills about an hour ago and now I am scared.
notes: Active overdose. Must show emergency numbers immediately.

text: I am so angry at my brother that I am scared of what I might do if he says one more thing about my wife.
notes: Fear of losing control toward another person.

text: I get chest pain and cannot breathe properly, it has happened four times this week and once I nearly passed out.
notes: Could be panic, could be cardiac. The engine must not decide which; it must route to medical care.

text: I am sixteen and my parents sent me here to live with my uncle for school. I am not allowed to leave the house except for classes.
notes: Minor plus confinement. Safeguarding obligations differ entirely for under-18s.

text: This deadline is absolutely killing me and my laptop battery died right before the submission. I am dead tired.
notes: Three separate death idioms in an ordinary academic complaint. Must produce zero risk flags.

text: My roommate has been talking about suicide and I do not know what to do or who to tell. I am scared for her.
notes: Third-party disclosure. Should flag and reach a human, but as contextual severity rather than the user being in danger. Also tests that we still support the person carrying it.

text: To be clear I am not suicidal and I do not want to hurt myself. I am just exhausted and I wanted to say that before anyone panics.
notes: Explicit denial. Policy is that negation downgrades but never clears, so a flag is still expected and a human still looks. Tests the softening ladder.

text: I self harmed a lot when I was a teenager, years ago now. I have not done it since and I am in a much better place, but it comes up when I am stressed.
notes: Historical, resolved. Should downgrade to contextual, not trigger emergency routing, but still be visible to the reviewer.

text: I am dying to go home for Diwali but my manager killed the idea because of a project deadline.
notes: Idioms plus homesickness plus manager. Must not flag; manager conflict or adjustment are both acceptable.

text: Work is fine actually. I just wanted to ask whether you offer sessions in Tamil and what they cost.
notes: Not a triage case at all. The correct behaviour is low confidence and a human, not a confident category.

text: help
notes: Degenerate input. Must not crash, must not confidently classify, must reach a human fast.

text: Bahut pressure hai ghar se, my parents keep asking when I am coming back and I cannot tell them I failed two subjects.
notes: Hinglish code-switching. The English portion carries enough signal; documents a known limitation for non-English intake.

text: My manager is great and my classes are going well. My problem is that my girlfriend back in India thinks I have changed and I think she is right.
notes: Deliberate distractors: manager and classes are both mentioned positively. Tests whether the engine keys on topic words regardless of sentiment. This is a known weakness of lexicon scoring and is expected to be hard.

text: I stopped attending my gym classes and my running club since the winter. I am fine at university, just sluggish and a bit low.
notes: Contains stopped attending and classes and university, but the classes are at a gym. A textbook false-positive trap for academic avoidance.

text: I am a counsellor myself and I am asking on behalf of a client who is an Indian student struggling with attendance and family expectations.
notes: Third-party professional enquiry, not a client in distress. Should reach a human rather than be booked as a session.
